title: Transitivity on bounded constructible complexes
statement:
For a prime $\ell$, a scheme $X$ and finite extensions $E\le F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside
$\Qlb$, the natural isomorphism

$$
T_{F,\Qlb}\circ T_{E,F}\;\cong\;T_{E,\Qlb}\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)\longrightarrow
D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)
$$

of functors between bounded constructible categories
([def-sfb-constructible-extend-subfield], [def-sfb-constructible-extend-to-qlbar]) is the
restriction of the isomorphism of [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso].

proof.text: Write $C_E=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ and $C_\Omega=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$, with inclusions $i_E$ and $i_\Omega$ into their ambient derived categories. These are full subcategories by [def-sfb-dcons-subfield] and [def-sfb-dcons-qlbar]: the arrows between two of their objects are precisely the ambient arrows, with the same identities and composition. Let $A=T_{F,\Qlb}\circ T_{E,F}$ and $B=T_{E,\Qlb}$ denote the restricted functors $C_E\to C_\Omega$. By [def-sfb-constructible-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-constructible-extend-to-qlbar], their underlying objects and maps are those of the corresponding ambient composite and direct extension, restricted along $i_E$. In particular both endpoints of every component of the ambient comparison belong to $C_\Omega$.

source.place: First sentence: identify the two restricted functors after inclusion in the ambient derived category.

proof.text: Let $\theta$ be the ambient natural isomorphism of [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso]. For $K\in C_E$, define $\alpha_K:A(K)\to B(K)$ to be the arrow of the full subcategory whose underlying arrow is $\theta_{i_EK}$. Define $\beta_K:B(K)\to A(K)$ in the same way from $\theta_{i_EK}^{-1}$. The endpoints are those checked in step 1, so these are actual arrows of $C_\Omega$; no choice of an object or of a new isomorphism is involved. The equalities $\theta_{i_EK}^{-1}\circ\theta_{i_EK}=\mathrm{id}_{A(K)}$ and $\theta_{i_EK}\circ\theta_{i_EK}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{B(K)}$ hold in the full subcategory because its composition and identity are the ambient ones. Thus $\alpha_K$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\beta_K$.

source.place: First sentence and second sentence: use the ambient isomorphism and lift its components through the full inclusion.

proof.text: For an arrow $u:K\to L$ in $C_E$, naturality of the comparison $\theta$ of [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso] gives $B(u)\circ\alpha_K=\alpha_L\circ A(u)$ on underlying ambient arrows. Since the Hom sets of $C_\Omega$ are those ambient Hom sets, this is the naturality equation in $C_\Omega$. Naturality of $\theta^{-1}$ gives $A(u)\circ\beta_K=\beta_L\circ B(u)$ on underlying ambient arrows; the equality of Hom sets makes this the naturality equation for $\beta$ in $C_\Omega$. The componentwise inverse identities of step 2 therefore make $\alpha:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ a natural isomorphism. After $i_\Omega$ its components are exactly those of $\theta$ restricted along $i_E$, so it is the restriction specified in the statement. Any other lift with that image has the same underlying component at every $K$, hence the same component in the full subcategory; it equals $\alpha$.

source.place: Second sentence: write out naturality, the inverse identities and uniqueness of the lifted natural isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: The complete proof paragraph, expanded on full-subcategory Hom sets, component inverses, naturality and uniqueness.
